result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy values via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (which strips `https?://` and paths), while the reader compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host` (a bare hostname). The old spec fixture even shows values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` were valid legacy settings, and line 31 deletes the site settings, making the data loss unrecoverable. Verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — FORMAT-DRIFT between writer paths: the migration inserts each legacy `embeddable_hosts` line verbatim (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no scheme/path/CR stripping, while the only other writer (EmbeddableHost#before_validation, embeddable_host.rb:6-7) strips `https?://` and `/...`, and the reader (`where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, embeddable_host.rb:17) compares a bare hostname; legacy values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (both accepted by the deleted SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? and used as valid fixtures in the pre-diff spec) land in the table unnormalized and never match any referer, and line 31 deletes the site setting so existing installs lose embedding on deploy with no way to recover the original list (severity P1, confidence 85, blocking)
